quote: Oh, we can definitely help you out. 700? Alright.
stewart_read: The customer just disclosed a $700+ monthly bill — a strong pain point — and the rep acknowledges it generically then moves straight to the next verify item (roof type) without flipping it into urgency or curiosity about savings.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be strategically saving the bill number for the closer to use as the emotional centerpiece of the proposal walkthrough.
coaching_implication: This hypothesis is weakly supported — the schema requires the flip to happen at setter stage regardless of what the closer later does with the number, since the setter's job is to build curiosity that carries into the appointment. Coach the rep to add one line tying the bill to savings potential before moving on, e.g. reflecting the number back with a comparison-forward framing.

quote: Is there anybody else on the title?
stewart_read: The transcript here is garbled and appears to mix rep and customer lines (diarization artifact) — the customer's reply, 'somebody else is doing a deed,' does not clearly establish who else may be on title or make a decision. It is ambiguous whether this indicates a co-owner requiring inclusion per protocols.spouse_decision or protocols.adult_child_decision_maker, or is simply transcription noise.
alternative_hypothesis: The line could be a genuine disclosure of a second title-holder the rep should have probed further, or it could be an artifact of poor audio/diarization with no real signal at all.
coaching_implication: Because the transcript is unreliable here, the manager should listen to the raw audio at this timestamp before drawing conclusions — do not coach the rep on a specific protocol miss until the actual exchange is confirmed.

quote: Because the, the light bill is actually in my daughter's name.
stewart_read: This is a distinct disclosure from the earlier 01:15 'deed' comment — it may or may not be the same person referenced earlier, but the rep does not probe whether the daughter is a co-owner, a co-decision-maker, or simply the utility account holder. Any connection between this and the earlier title comment is speculative and should not be treated as confirmed.
alternative_hypothesis: The daughter may just be the utility account holder with no ownership or decision-making role, making this a non-issue.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to ask a quick clarifying question ('Is she on the home's title too, or just the power bill?') any time a third-party name surfaces mid-call, so the closer has clean information rather than an ambiguous thread.

quote: Actually, a couple of people on my block didn't get them put in. That's that's another reason why I was wondering about it because a lot of people on my block been lately getting it put in.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers neighborhood social proof as a second interest driver beyond the bill, unprompted. This is a second qualifying reason the rep could reinforce when booking the appointment.
coaching_implication: The rep should have acknowledged this and could have used it in the button-up or text follow-up ('since your neighbors are looking into it too...') to personalize the appointment tieback, but did not reference it again.

quote: When he had discussed the about how much it'll be.
stewart_read: Customer asks a pricing question right at the close of the call. The rep does not quote a number but redirects to the specialist's comparison walkthrough, which is a reasonable strategy match to the price_estimate_before_design rebuttal even though the phrasing is looser than the canonical script.
coaching_implication: This is a positive example to reinforce with the rep — he held scope and avoided fabricating numbers under a live pricing question. Point to this moment as the model to repeat.

quote: Alright. We got that. And then what's, what's a good week for you guys? Next week or this week?
stewart_read: The rep moves into scheduling without a clean transition or recap of what was just gathered, and the eventual button-up (09:08-09:14) skips the one-hour block framing, the no-driving/computer instruction, and the 'is that fair?' handshake entirely.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to run the full button-up checklist verbatim or in close paraphrase every time — the appointment was booked but the mechanics that predict show-rate (hour-block framing, computer/no-driving ask, verbal handshake) were never stated.

quote: Do you get your power bill in the mail or online?
stewart_read: Despite a mid-collection complication (bill in daughter's name), the rep kept the bill-collection sequence moving from ask to text-sent to bill-received in roughly two and a half minutes (03:30 to 06:13), which is efficient relative to the schema's flagged 8-15 minute time-burn failure pattern.
coaching_implication: This is worth noting as competent execution — the rep didn't panic or over-explain when the ownership-name complication came up, and kept the call moving. Reinforce this pacing as a strength.
